simple.meaning: אַיֶּלֶת (ʼayeleth) is a Hebrew word meaning “a doe.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אַיֶּלֶת (H365) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Psalms 22:1, with occurrences in Psalms, Proverbs, Jeremiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אַיֶּלֶת (H365) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אַיֶּלֶת (H365) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אַיֶּלֶת (ʼayeleth) / H365 is traced through Psalms 22:1, Proverbs 5:19, Jeremiah 14:5 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

occurrences.englishText: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?
A loving doe and a graceful deer—
Yes, the doe in the field also calves and forsakes her young,
